evidence_policy.official_inference: Reasonable diagnostic conclusion derived from Ring documentation, but not a literal Ring statement.
evidence_policy.contextual_only: Project telemetry that may support diagnosis but has no Ring-published threshold in the reviewed documentation.
evidence_policy.engineering: Project-specific heuristic. Must never be presented as an official Ring threshold.
evidence_policy.unverified: Content attributed to Ring whose source has not been verified by this project (source titles have no URLs). Must never be presented as official Ring documentation. `declared_evidence_level` keeps the level the article originally claimed; `verification` and `source_verification` mark individual unverified or pending items.

issues.title: Weak or Unstable Wi-Fi Signal
symptoms: Slow or intermittent Live View
Low quality video
Poor audio quality
Device frequently disconnecting
Intermittent service dropouts
Device shows as offline

official_signals.interpretation: Great
Okay
Poor
Very poor

official_facts: Ring states that a weak Wi-Fi signal can cause low-quality video.
Ring states that a weak Wi-Fi signal can cause a device to fall offline.
Ring classifies RSSI of -80 dBm or worse as very poor.
Ring identifies distance, walls, brick, stucco, metal, mirrors and electronic equipment as factors that can weaken Wi-Fi.
issues.contextual_metric_policy: Use these metrics as supporting evidence only. Do not apply an invented Ring threshold.
recommended_actions: Check Signal Strength in Ring Device Health.

issues.title: Insufficient Ring Device Transmit Speed
symptoms: Connectivity issues
Device offline
Low video quality
Slow video loading
Stream freezing or dropouts during playback

official_signals.interpretation: GOOD
OKAY
POOR

official_facts: Ring states that Device Transmit Speed measures the speed between the Ring device and router.
Ring classifies Device Transmit Speed above 20 Mbps as GOOD.
Ring classifies Device Transmit Speed between 10 and 20 Mbps as OKAY.
Ring classifies Device Transmit Speed below 10 Mbps as POOR.
Ring states that poor transmit speed can cause connectivity issues, offline status, or low video quality.
recommended_actions: Check Device Transmit Speed in Ring Device Health.
Move the Ring device closer to the Wi-Fi router.
Verify there are no dense walls or metal obstructions between device and router.
Consider a Ring Chime Pro or Wi-Fi mesh node.
Check if other devices on the network are saturating bandwidth.
Restart router and Ring device.
official_sources: Finding your Ring device's transmit speed

customer_messages.default: Your doorbell can't send video fast enough, so live video may stutter. Restart your router and move it closer to the doorbell, then check Device Health in the Ring app.

issues.title: Insufficient Internet Upload Speed
symptoms: Slow video loading
Video stream freezing or stuttering
Poor audio quality
Device disconnecting
Failed Live View attempts

official_signals.interpretation: GOOD
OKAY
POOR

official_facts: Ring states that Internet Upload Speed measures the speed from your router to the internet.
Ring classifies Internet Upload Speed above 10 Mbps as GOOD.
Ring classifies Internet Upload Speed between 5 and 10 Mbps as OKAY.
Ring classifies Internet Upload Speed below 5 Mbps as POOR.
Ring states that poor upload speed can cause slow video, freezing, poor audio, or disconnections.
recommended_actions: Check Internet Upload Speed in Ring Device Health.

Disconnect unnecessary devices using high upload bandwidth (cloud backups, torrents).
Contact your Internet Service Provider (ISP) to verify upstream bandwidth.

official_api_mapping.verification: unverified: used by this project's read-only client (src/utils/ring_partner_client.py), but not re-verified against Ring documentation in this environment

issues.title: Poor Video Quality, Blurry, Washed Out, or Overexposed
symptoms: Blurry or out-of-focus image
Washed out, bleached, or excessively bright picture
Dark or underexposed video
Pixelated or blocky video artifacts
Distorted colors or magenta/pink tint
Dirty or smudged lens view
Low sharpness score during inspection
official_facts: Ring states that weak Wi-Fi signal can cause pixelated and degraded video streams.
Ring states that dirty or smudged optical lenses cause blur, fog, and light glare.
Ring notes that direct sunlight shining into the camera lens can cause severe overexposure.
Ring cameras adjust exposure automatically based on lighting conditions in the field of view.
A stuck mechanical IR cut filter causes a pink or purple discoloration in daylight.
Condensation or moisture inside or outside the lens housing degrades optical sharpness.
issues.important_constraint: No Ring-published threshold was established for bitrate, FPS or OpenCV sharpness in the reviewed documentation.

Check Wi-Fi signal strength (RSSI) in Ring Device Health.
Inspect physical mounting angle; adjust with a Wedge or Corner Kit to avoid direct sunlight or bright walls.
Power cycle the device to reset the mechanical IR cut filter if pink tint is observed.
Check for condensation or physical lens scratches.
Ensure lens protective shipping film was peeled off during initial installation.
Verify adequate lighting in the monitored area.
official_sources: Understanding Wi-Fi recommendations for Ring devices

customer_messages.default: Your doorbell's picture looks blurry or unclear, which can hide details in your videos. Gently clean the camera lens with a soft, dry cloth, then check the live view in the Ring app.

Live View times out after 10-15 seconds of buffering

official_facts: Ring states that weak Wi-Fi signal is the primary cause of Live View timeouts and failed connections.
Ring requires a minimum 2 Mbps upload and download speed per 1080p device (4 Mbps for 4K/Pro models).
Active Ring Protect subscription or trial is required to view historical video recordings in the cloud.
Aggressive router firewalls or blocked WebRTC ports (UDP 10000-20000, TCP 8555/443) prevent video egress.
Ring devices enter deep sleep or low-power state if battery drops below critical threshold (e.g., < 10%).
WebRTC / WHEP session tokens expire after duration limits or when conflicting sessions open simultaneously.

Very Poor Wi-Fi category as cited by KB-RING-001 (source pending verification).

recommended_actions: Check RSSI and Wi-Fi health in Ring Device Health.
Verify device battery level or hardwired transformer power supply.
Confirm active Ring Home / Ring Protect plan for event history playback.
Check router firewall settings and ensure outbound WebRTC/UDP traffic is permitted.
Reboot router and test connection using Ring app on mobile cellular data.
Power cycle the Ring doorbell or camera.

issues.title: Night Vision, Color, IR Filter, or Glare Issues
symptoms: Black and white image during daylight hours
Pink or magenta hue across daytime video
Unnatural or distorted color rendering
Pitch black video at night despite nominal Wi-Fi network
White glare halo or light reflection washout at night
Image washed out by infrared light reflecting off adjacent wall or roof eave
official_facts: Ring devices automatically adapt their night vision according to available ambient light.
Some Ring devices switch to infrared black-and-white imaging in low light conditions.
Color Night Vision requires ambient lighting (e.g. porch light, street lamp) to synthesize color.
Infrared LEDs reflecting off a nearby wall, siding, brick, or overhang will blind the sensor and cause washouts.
A stuck internal IR cut filter prevents the camera from returning to standard color mode in daylight.
High-contrast scenes (bright sunny background with dark porch) challenge dynamic range adjustments.
Covering or obstructing the ambient light sensor triggers night mode prematurely.
LED porch lights operating on PWM can produce optical stroboscopic bands.
recommended_actions: Check Wi-Fi signal strength in Ring Device Health.
Verify the monitored area has adequate ambient light for Color Night Vision.
Install a Wedge or Corner Kit to aim the camera away from adjacent walls or reflective surfaces.
Power cycle the Ring device to unstick the mechanical IR filter.
Toggle Color Night Vision off and on in Ring app Video Settings.
Gently wipe down the lens and infrared emitter array with a microfiber cloth.
official_sources: Using Mounting Accessories (Corner Kit and Wedge Kit)

customer_messages.default: Your doorbell's daytime picture looks pink or purple, which can happen when the night-vision filter is stuck. Check the live view in the Ring app again in a few minutes; if the colours stay wrong, contact Ring Support.

issues.title: Missing Audio or Two-Way Talk Issues
symptoms: User cannot hear audio from visitor at the door
Visitor cannot hear user speaking through Ring device
Complete silence during Live View and cloud recordings
Audio is muted or muffled
Recorded event videos have no sound track
Severe voice delay, audio jitter, or acoustic feedback echo
official_facts: Ring documents no audio during Live View or recorded events when microphone permissions are denied.
Ring documents situations where the user cannot hear a visitor or the visitor cannot hear the user.
Microphone toggle and speaker toggle in the Ring app control two-way stream audio transmission.
Severe packet loss or jitter over Wi-Fi causes audio dropouts and acoustic distortion.
Dirty or water-clogged microphone pinholes muffle incoming sound.
Two-Way Talk uses full-duplex WebRTC audio; low network bandwidth forces audio codecs to drop frames.
issues.contextual_metric_policy: WebRTC statistics may support an engineering diagnosis, but Ring thresholds for packet loss, jitter and RTT must not be invented.
recommended_actions: Check phone/tablet volume and ensure mute switch is off.
Check Ring microphone permissions in mobile device OS settings.
Verify speaker and microphone icons are unmuted in Live View screen.
Inspect physical Ring device; ensure microphone holes and speaker grille are clean and dry.
Check Wi-Fi signal strength (RSSI) and network packet loss.
Test Two-Way Talk on mobile cellular data to rule out local network multicast/SIP filtering.
Power cycle the Ring device.
official_sources: Live View for doorbells and cameras

issues.title: Solar Panel Not Charging Ring Doorbell or Camera Battery
symptoms: Doorbell battery discharges despite solar panel being plugged in
Device Health reports Solar Status as 'Not Connected' or disconnected
Battery percentage never rises above 90%
Device switches to battery saver mode during daylight hours

official_signals.interpretation: Normal documented behavior: Ring solar chargers do not start charging if battery exceeds 90% to protect lithium-ion lifespan.
Critically low battery with solar panel connected: possible solar shading, loose cable, or unsupported accessory.
Insufficient voltage detected on solar charging circuit.

official_facts: Ring states that Solar Chargers and Solar Panels require at least 3 to 4 hours of direct sunlight daily to maintain battery charge.
Ring states that solar chargers will not begin charging the battery until the charge level drops below 90% to preserve lithium-ion battery health.
Extreme temperatures (below 0°C / 32°F or above 48°C / 120°F) halt solar charging to protect internal battery cells.
Solar panels provide a trickle charge to maintain battery level; they cannot instantly recharge a completely depleted battery.
Dust, pollen, snow, or tree debris covering solar photovoltaic cells drastically reduces power output.

official_api_mapping.verification: unverified: the client reads /v1/devices only for discovery; these attributes are not confirmed by the documentation reviewed by this project and are not read by it

recommended_actions: Verify battery charge is below 90%; above this threshold the solar panel remains idle by design.
Ensure the solar panel receives at least 3 to 4 hours of unshaded direct sunlight daily.
Clean the solar panel surface with a damp soft cloth to remove dust and debris.
Inspect the micro-USB / barrel jack connector and ensure it is firmly seated and weather-sealed.
If battery is fully depleted, remove it and charge to 100% via wall outlet before reconnecting solar.
official_sources: Troubleshooting Solar Chargers and Solar Panels for Ring Doorbells
Ring Help Center: Extreme temperatures and battery charging

issues.title: Ethernet Link Loss or Power Failure on Ring Video Doorbell Elite (PoE)
symptoms: Ring Doorbell Elite appears offline in the app despite LED ring being lit
PoE switch port shows no data link activity (link LED off)
Device reboots intermittently whenever a call or Live View is started
Total loss of network connectivity after switching router or PoE injector

official_signals.interpretation: Incompatible: Ring Elite requires active IEEE 802.3af or 802.3at standard (48V nominal). Passive PoE causes instability or hardware damage.
Severe packet loss on Ethernet cabling: damaged Cat5e/Cat6 cable or improperly crimped RJ45 plug.

official_facts: Ring Video Doorbell Elite is powered exclusively by Power over Ethernet (PoE) and requires standard IEEE 802.3af or 802.3at compliant switches or injectors.
Ring specifies that passive PoE or non-standard injectors can power the LED ring but fail to deliver sufficient current during video transmission, leading to brownout reboot loops.
Ethernet cable runs exceeding 100 meters (328 ft) or damaged Cat5e/Cat6 pairs cause link negotiation drops and voltage sag.
PoE negotiation relies on 48V active handshake; unmanaged switches with power budget exhaustion drop port power under load.

official_api_mapping.verification: unverified: the client reads /v1/devices only for discovery; these attributes are not confirmed by the documentation reviewed by this project and are not read by it

recommended_actions: Verify PoE switch or injector strictly complies with the IEEE 802.3af or 802.3at standard (48V active PoE).
Disconnect Ethernet cable from PoE injector/switch for 30 seconds and reconnect to power cycle the port.
Test Ethernet cable continuity with a RJ45 cable tester to verify all 8 conductors are intact.
Check PoE switch power budget to confirm the port has at least 15.4W allocated for the Elite doorbell.
official_sources: Ring Video Doorbell Elite Setup and Power Specifications

issues.title: In-Home Mechanical or Digital Chime Not Ringing on Doorbell Press
issues.source_verification: pending: official_sources are Ring Help Center article titles without URLs; the 16 VAC figure and the configurations endpoint mapping have not been re-verified against Ring documentation by this project.
symptoms: Exterior Ring doorbell rings and sends app notification, but indoor house chime does not ring
Indoor chime emits a continuous hum or buzz without striking the tone bell
Indoor chime rings weakly, intermittently, or with distorted tones

official_signals.interpretation: Project diagnostic rule for mechanical chimes (not a Ring-published threshold): transformer voltage may be insufficient to power both the doorbell electronics and the chime solenoid.
Setting disabled in Ring App: In-Home Chime Type configured as None/Disabled.

official_facts: Ring doorbells require the correct In-Home Chime Type setting in the Ring App: Mechanical (solenoid chime) or Digital (electronic melody chime).

In hardwired installations, when the doorbell button is pressed, the Ring device bridges the circuit; insufficient transformer voltage under load can make a mechanical solenoid hum instead of striking (this project flags it below 16 VAC as a product diagnostic rule, not a Ring specification).
Digital electronic chimes require setting a chime ring duration (typically 2 to 5 seconds) to play the chime audio file.
Failure to install the included Pro Power Kit or terminal jumper can cause chime humming and damage the transformer.

recommended_actions: Open Ring App, navigate to Device Settings > In-Home Chime Settings, and verify Mechanical or Digital chime is selected.
For digital chimes, verify ring duration setting in the app allows sufficient time to play the full melody.
Inspect in-home chime transformer voltage under load (project rule for mechanical chimes: 16 VAC or more).
Verify terminal wiring and confirm Pro Power Kit / jumper wire is installed correctly across chime terminals.
Check chime compatibility list on Ring Help Center to ensure chime model is supported.

issues.title: Flickering or Horizontal Video Banding from LED Lighting (50Hz / 60Hz)
symptoms: Flickering horizontal dark bands or rolling lines moving across Live View video
Stroboscopic effect visible in video whenever porch light or fixture is illuminated
Video stream is crisp and clean when porch illumination is switched off

official_signals.interpretation: Excellent network and WebRTC metrics: flickering does NOT originate from packet loss or insufficient bandwidth.
Rolling shutter stroboscopic banding detected on optical CMOS sensor matching AC power grid frequency of 50Hz or 60Hz.

official_facts: Ring explains that flickering horizontal dark bands (banding) are caused by the optical rolling shutter sensor syncing with pulse-width modulated (PWM) LED porch lights.
Discrepancies between camera anti-flicker frequency (50 Hz in Europe/UK vs 60 Hz in Americas) and domestic AC grid frequency generate visible strobe artifacts.
Cheap or non-dimmable LED bulbs operating on dimmer switches exacerbate electrical ripple and optical flicker.
Anti-flicker algorithm adjusts sensor shutter speed to an exact multiple of the AC line power frequency.

official_api_mapping.verification: path matches Ring's official API documentation (developer.amazon.com/docs/ring/api-documentation.html, checked on 2026-10-21); the fields listed in relevant_data are not verified by this project, and the endpoint is not implemented here (the client only uses /v1/devices, /status and /capabilities)

recommended_actions: Check if flickering ceases when turning off porch light or nearby lamp fixture.
In Ring camera Video Settings, adjust Anti-Flicker mode to match local power grid (50 Hz for Europe/UK, 60 Hz for Americas).
Replace low-cost or non-regulated LED porch bulbs with high-quality flicker-free LED fixtures.
Ensure porch light dimmer switches are set to 100% or use dimmable-rated LED driver units.
official_sources: Video flickering or banding on Ring Doorbells and Security Cameras
Ring Developer Experience: Video Pipeline Specifications

customer_messages.default: Your video shows flickering stripes, usually caused by a nearby LED light. Try switching that light off or using a different bulb, then check the live view in the Ring app.

issues.title: WebRTC / WHEP Live View Negotiation Failure or E2EE Block
issues.source_verification: pending: official_sources are titles without URLs; the WHEP, E2EE, host and scope details in this article have not been verified by this project, and WHEP is not implemented.
symptoms: Streaming error 'Streaming could not be started' or 'Live View unavailable' when requesting WHEP session
A WHEP session request responds with 400 Bad Request or 409 Conflict (endpoint not verified by this project)
Screen remains black with infinite loading indicator in third-party API integrations
Camera has End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) enabled and API rejects stream request

official_signals.interpretation: Device has active E2EE: video stream via Ring Partner API cannot be decrypted on cloud servers or via API without client device private key.
Excessive latency in WebRTC SDP handshake: timeout negotiating data channel and STUN/TURN packets.

official_facts: Ring's API release notes document live video streaming using the WHEP (WebRTC HTTP Egress Protocol) standard and RTSP; the session details in this article are unverified by this project, and WHEP is not implemented here.
WHEP sessions require an SDP offer sent with Content-Type: application/sdp and Bearer OAuth authorization.
End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) on Ring devices encrypts video at the edge using customer-managed keys; cloud WHEP endpoints cannot proxy unencrypted streams when E2EE is active.
Only one active WHEP streaming session is permitted per camera simultaneously; concurrent requests yield 409 Conflict.
SDP offer must include DTLS-SRTP fingerprints and ICE candidate trickling support.

Ring's API documentation limits live streams to up to 30 seconds on battery-powered devices and up to 60 seconds on line-powered devices; media is receive-only (recvonly: video, plus one-way audio when requested) and two-way media is not supported.
Multi-camera Ring hubs require specifying the component_id parameter in the WHEP URL.

official_api_mapping.verification: path matches Ring's official API documentation (developer.amazon.com/docs/ring/api-documentation.html, checked on 2026-10-21); the other session details in this article are not verified by this project; WHEP is not implemented here and the Digital Twin WHEP answer is simulated

path matches Ring's official API documentation (developer.amazon.com/docs/ring/api-documentation.html, checked on 2026-10-21); the fields listed in relevant_data are not verified by this project, and the endpoint is not implemented here (the client only uses /v1/devices, /status and /capabilities)

recommended_actions: Check if End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) is enabled in the Ring App; third-party APIs cannot access live streams without client-side key decryption.
For multi-camera devices or Ring Elite, ensure 'component_id' query parameter is specified in the WHEP URL.
Confirm no other client or Ring App session is actively streaming from the camera to avoid 409 Conflict.
Verify the Ring Partner OAuth 2.0 access token is not expired and has the streaming permission Ring requires (the scope name is not verified by this project).
Check local firewall allows outbound UDP traffic on WebRTC ports (10000-20000) and ICE STUN/TURN binding.
Retry session creation with refreshed SDP offer after closing orphan WHEP sessions.

Ring Developer Experience: Live Streaming Architecture
Ring Partner API Security and End-to-End Encryption Specifications
